newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold ends down despite shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends down despite shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended a shade lower from New York's previous close after losses from morning sales were marginally recouped by afternoon shortcovering, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$351.30/80 an ounce on Thursday against New York's US$351.80/352.30 close on Wednesday.
Some dealers said Japanese and Australian selling in the morning had depressed gold slightly and sentiment was bearish.
Overseas buying started in Hong Kong's afternoon session, some bullion dealers said, noting shortcovering.
But others said the main focus remained on silver.
Physical buying was lukewarm, sources said.
Local gold ended HK$21 lower at HK$3,251 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous level at -4.00.
